reason:
Verified verbatim by driving, and the strings are exactly what the finding claims.

THE CODE. render-b.js closeRun() (lines 251-262) writes one template for every member of a run: " " + unit + ", " + (i === 0 ? "first" : "then") + " of " + run.length + " moments on this day,". The word "then" is substituted where an ordinal belongs, so member 2 of a run renders " days away, then of 2 moments on this day,". b.css:326-327 sets .b-item[data-stack="follow"] .b-away, .b-tick { visibility: hidden } - visibility:hidden removes a node from the accessibility tree, so the follower's numeral is not spoken at all. The unit is left behind in the .b-vh span with nothing in front of it.

DRIVEN, THE FINDING'S OWN PATH. state=owner-editing at 1440x960; press +7 on "Send the invitations" until the stepper goes aria-disabled=true at the ceiling. It lands on 3 October beside the wedding day. Playwright ariaSnapshot of .b-measure returns, character for character:
  listitem: text "79 days away, first of 2 moments on this day," / "Send the invitations" / "Sat 3 Oct"
  listitem: text "days away, then of 2 moments on this day," / "Wedding day" / "Sat 3 Oct"
The follower carries NO number in the AX tree - the claimed string is exact. The gate's own route reproduces it too: a single press of "Move a week earlier" stacks at away=16 and gives "days away, then of 2 moments on this day,". Two independent routes, one press and twelve presses, both land it. Note which row loses its figure on the ceiling route: the wedding day itself, the one row in the product that must never be ambiguous, reaches a listening reader with no distance on it.

NOT A GATE RESTATEMENT. interaction-check.mjs:2317 asserts "the day says how many it holds" as a /2 moments on this day/ test against stacked.said, which is the two rows JOINED with " / ". The lead alone satisfies it, so the assertion passes while the follower reads as nonsense. The gate is blind to precisely the half the finding is about. The only other spoken-unit assertion, line 296 "every row speaks its unit", runs on state=phone at rest, and I confirmed by driving that NO state renders a stack at rest - phone, desk, day, print, unfurl, ended and owner-flight all return zero lead/follow rows - so that gate never sees a run either.

NOT SETTLED, NOT A RE-RAISE. The round-notes "one of three wording" refusal is the project switcher in the header (round-8 brand--one-of-three-has-no-noun), a different string on a different component. The reverse holds: this is a REGRESSION AGAINST THE PANEL'S OWN PRIOR RULING. round-2 verdicts/same-day-stack-undesigned.json sharpened the fix and specified the spoken form in terms - lead "days away, first of 2 moments on this day," and follower "days away, 2nd of 2 moments on this day,". The build took the lead half and substituted "then" for the ordinal on the follower. The panel already paid for this string once.

NO CONSTRAINT IS TOUCHED. It is visually-hidden text: no hue, no weight, no family, no architecture, no reparenting, no change to any drawn pixel or to place()'s geometry. The visible gutter is correct as it stands and the fix does not touch it.

WHERE THE FINDING'S OWN FIX IS WRONG, AND WHY IT STILL CONFIRMS. Its follower string drops "days away" entirely ("the same day, the second of 2 moments on it"). That throws away the distance figure visibility:hidden has already taken from the follower, and it puts the copy on a collision course with the line-296 invariant the moment any fixture holds a same-day pair at rest. Confirmed on the defect; take the sharpened fix below instead.
sharpenedFix:
In closeRun(), keep the shape but give the follower back the number the gutter took from it, and give both members a real ordinal. Add beside the function: var ORDINAL = ["first", "second", "third", "fourth", "fifth"]; and function nth(i) { return ORDINAL[i] || (i + 1) + "th"; }. Then:

  said.textContent = run.length === 1
    ? " " + unit + ","
    : (i === 0 ? " " : " " + el.getAttribute("data-away") + " ")
      + unit + ", the " + nth(i) + " of " + run.length + " moments on this day,";

The lead keeps its visible numeral and reads "79 days away, the first of 2 moments on this day, Wedding day, Sat 3 Oct". The follower, whose numeral is visibility:hidden and therefore unspoken, supplies the figure in the hidden span and reads "79 days away, the second of 2 moments on this day, ..." - symmetrical with the lead, never a unit without a number in front of it, and the distance is not lost to a reader arrowing row by row who gets none of the adjacency a sighted reader gets for free. Every row still carries "days away" in its textContent, so line 296's invariant holds for any future fixture that stacks at rest, and line 2317's existing test still matches - now on both members rather than only on the lead.

Then sharpen the gate so this cannot come back. Change "the day says how many it holds" to collect the members' strings as a LIST rather than a joined string, and assert that every one of them matches a pattern requiring one or more digits, then " days away, the ", then first|second, then " of 2 moments on this day,". Add one cheap global assertion alongside it: across every state, no .b-unitSaid may begin with whitespace followed immediately by the word "days" (a unit with no figure in front of it), and none may contain the substring " then of ". Both are one line each and they close the exact blind spot that let "then of 2" ship.
